sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Define an organization.
questions.answer: A social unit created with a specific purpose.

questions.q: Distinguish open and closed systems in one line each.
questions.answer: A closed system does not interact with its environment; an open system continuously interacts through input, transformation, output and feedback.

questions.q: Name any two inputs of an organization.
questions.answer: Human resource, capital, technology, material, information (any two).

questions.q: Name any three subsystems of an organization.
questions.answer: Goal, technical, managerial, structural, psychological (any three).

questions.q: Define organizational climate.
questions.answer: The relatively enduring atmosphere of an organization's internal environment experienced by its members, influencing their performance.

questions.q: Name the four determinants of climate.
questions.answer: Organizational structure, technology, external environment and management policies and practices.

questions.q: Name the four leadership styles.
questions.answer: Authoritarian, paternalistic, consultative and participative.

questions.q: State true or false: (i) Work is a social activity. (ii) In authoritarian relationship employees are fully involved in goals.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False.

questions.q: Name the four strategies for developing productivity.
questions.answer: Selection and placement, training and development, task design, performance appraisal and rewards.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Name the subsystem: (i) goals and objectives; (ii) knowledge and equipment; (iii) planning and coordination; (iv) social relationships and norms.
questions.answer: (i) Goal. (ii) Technical. (iii) Managerial. (iv) Psychological.

questions.q: Identify the leadership style: (i) threats and punishment; (ii) some participation but rewards and threats; (iii) goals set after consultation; (iv) full involvement and two-way communication.
questions.answer: (i) Authoritarian. (ii) Paternalistic. (iii) Consultative. (iv) Participative.

questions.q: Give the effect on climate: (i) assembly line technology; (ii) aerospace technology; (iii) severe economic conditions; (iv) autonomy and feedback by managers.
questions.answer: (i) Rigid, low trust. (ii) Trust and responsibility. (iii) Threatening climate. (iv) Achievement-oriented climate.

questions.q: Name four job design elements that improve performance.
questions.answer: Variety, autonomy, responsibility, feedback and task identity (any four).

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is feedback in an organization?
questions.answer: Information from the environment that helps the organization take suitable steps to meet its challenges and expectations.

questions.q: Why is an organization called an open system?
questions.answer: Because it is influenced by the environment and also influences it.

questions.q: What is the goal subsystem?
questions.answer: The overall goals and objectives of the organization and the goals of departments and individuals.

questions.q: What is organizational socialization?
questions.answer: The process by which an employee acquires the knowledge and skills needed to take a place in the organization.

questions.q: What is a psychological contract?
questions.answer: An unwritten shared understanding of the mutual expectations of employee and organization.

questions.q: What is role ambiguity?
questions.answer: Lack of clarity about job requirements and work objectives, which reduces productivity.

questions.q: What is excellence in an organization?
questions.answer: Performance exceeding minimum standards of effectiveness, bringing reputation.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the organization as an open system.
questions.answer: It takes inputs (human resource, capital, technology, material, information) from the environment, transforms them into outputs and receives feedback to meet environmental expectations.

questions.q: Describe any two subsystems.
questions.answer: Goal subsystem: overall and departmental goals matching society's goals; technical subsystem: the use of knowledge, equipment and technology by workers.

questions.q: Explain any two determinants of climate.
questions.answer: Structure: decentralised gives participation, centralised gives consistency; technology: assembly lines create rigid climate and dynamic technology creates trust.

questions.q: Explain leadership styles and their effect.
questions.answer: Authoritarian, paternalistic, consultative and participative. The more participative the boss, the greater the productivity and satisfaction and the lower the absenteeism and turnover.

questions.q: Describe relationship with co-workers.
questions.answer: It grows from common tastes rather than rules; peers teach unwritten rules, provide emotional outlet and increase job satisfaction and commitment.

questions.q: Explain role clarity.
questions.answer: Understanding of job requirements and objectives increases commitment and productivity; role ambiguity and role conflict reduce it.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Describe the organization as a system and its subsystems.
questions.answer: An organization is a social unit; open systems take inputs, transform and output, and use feedback. Subsystems: goal, technical, managerial, structural and psychological, each with a specific significance.

questions.q: List the determinants of organizational climate and explain them.
questions.answer: Structure (centralised or decentralised), technology (routine or dynamic), external environment (economic conditions) and management policies (autonomy and feedback). A positive climate gives satisfaction and productivity.

questions.q: Discuss interpersonal relationships at work, socialization and communication.
questions.answer: Superior–subordinate relations depend on leadership style (authoritarian to participative); co-worker relations give support; organizational socialization is continuous and two-way, based on a psychological contract; communication transfers meaning through symbols.

questions.q: Discuss the factors influencing productivity and strategies to develop it.
questions.answer: Factors: abilities, aptitudes, interests, role clarity and performance environment. Strategies: selection and placement, training and development, task design (variety, autonomy, feedback) and performance appraisal with rewards.
